objective_for_doctor:
Age: 26
Sex: M
Chief Complaint: expiratory wheezing

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I’m having expiratory wheezing and shortness of breath in a significant way. I also have a very itchy pink rash with lesions on the back of my neck, both biceps, my mouth, and my right ankle.
To help assess the urgency, have you noticed any swelling of your lips, tongue, or throat, or experienced dizziness, lightheadedness, nausea, or abdominal pain?
When did these symptoms first start, and did they come on suddenly or gradually over time?
In the few hours before your symptoms began, were you exposed to any potential triggers such as a new food, medication, insect sting, or new personal care product?
Yes—I ate dark-fleshed fish (such as tuna) or Swiss cheese before the reaction occurred.
Did anyone else who ate the same meal develop similar symptoms?
Along with the breathing difficulty and rash, are you experiencing facial flushing, a throbbing headache, palpitations, or gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea?
Yes—I have my cheeks suddenly turned red, and I have palpitations (my heart is beating fast, irregularly/missing a beat). I don’t know about any throbbing headache or gastrointestinal symptoms.
When you were eating the fish, did you notice an unusually peppery, bitter, or metallic taste?
[DDX] Scombroid poisoning, Anaphylaxis, Acute IgE-mediated food allergy, Histamine intolerance, Mast cell activation syndrome
